newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Minyuan takes over Beijing telecom firm.
newsitem.headline: Minyuan takes over Beijing telecom firm.

text.p: Hainan Minyuan Modern Agriculture Development Co said on Thursday it had been given approval by the Beijing city government to take over a telecommunications firm based in China's capital.

Minyuan said it is set to acquire the state-run Beijing Catch Communication Group, whose subsidiary in the United States, AVIC, is a U.S.-listed company, according to a notice published in the official Securities Times. It did not give the percentage of equity stake in AVIC held by Beijing Catch.
A spokesman for the Shenzhen-listed firm told the China Securities Bulletin the takeover plan was backed by the Beijing Municipal Science & Technology Commission.
He said that Minyuan was not required to pay for the takeover, which he said should be seen as a merger arranged by the Beijing city government.
Minyuan's board of directors will take over daily management of Beijing Catch after the takeover, he said.
The move is aimed at restructuring Beijing Catch into a joint-stock entity and diversifying Minyuan's operations, the spokesman said.
Minyuan, based in Haikou, the capital of the southern province of Hainan, is mainly involved in real estate, production of building materials and tourism.
Beijing Catch, primarily engaged in pager and mobile telephone services and real estate, has total assets valued at about 1.5 billion yuan, the spokesman said.
Beijing Catch's annual total profits averaged 100 million yuan in the past several years, he added. He declined to provide precise profit figures.
Minyuan expects to finalise the takeover plan within the year. The company's shareholders would meet in Haikou on October 21 to review it, he said.
Minyuan said in its interim report that, under Chinese accounting standards, its net profits soared to 97.86 million yuan in the first half of 1996 from 116,900 yuan the same period last year.

Minyuan said first-half earnings mainly stemmed from sales and rentals of real estate projects in Beijing, including the recently completed 40,000-sq-metre Minyuan Building. It expects to earn 380 million yuan in revenue from sales of the office building this year, the company said.

The interim report said Minyuan had a total of 559.6 million shares as of June 30 this year, including 254.8 million founder shares, 117.3 million legal person shares, 187.4 million class A shares and 26,000 staff shares.
